$comment: Build identity registry. Every address, offset, wire type and function name in this repository is only valid for the exact client build it was measured on, so a build must be identified before any of that evidence is reused. Identity is the full SHA-256 of Bin64/NewWorld.exe, never a short hash or a version string alone (AGENTS.md). Ghidra projects and corpora stay in the ignored reverse/builds/<sha256>/.

consequence.statement: The installed build differs from the analyzed build in version, SHA-256 and size. Every VA in client-functions.json, every offset in the client-map and the 423,579-range corpus are historical for this install until re-derived. Static analysis and the live server experiments must be re-measured against 30fe6461 before their conclusions are reused.
consequence.not_yet_done: Corrected 2026-10-25: a Ghidra project and a corpus DO exist for 30fe6461. reverse/builds/30fe6461.../ghproj holds an analyzed project (459 MB) and reverse/builds/30fe6461.../corpus holds 3,396 pseudocode shards covering 423,609 functions against 423,637 .pdata entries, meta.json pinning exe_sha256 30fe6461. What is still missing is per-message naming: no ladder body has been decoded from this corpus yet.

az-type-registry.json.fixed_regression: The first 1.460 regeneration used only the 1.400 brace form and lost 111 registry-sourced names (722 table-resident pairs vs 750 on 1.400), which broke scripts/inbound-inventory.py --check on wire 7048. The 1.460 form can carry pointer qwords between the name and the {GUID}; scan-az-types.py now reads that field-block form, giving 939 table-resident pairs against 722.

wire-type-names.json.note: Regenerated 2026-10-25 after fixing four defects in scan-wire-names.py, which had been unrunnable since private-client/ moved to the repo root. Named rose from 2239 to 2559: 391 real names gained, 71 removed, and ZERO names that were already correct changed slot. Of the 71 removed, 39 MOVED to the correct slot (the name survived, the GUID it was attached to was wrong) and 32 were fragments that belong to nobody.
defects_fixed: ROOT resolved to reverse/ instead of the repo root, so every path was one level too high and the tool raised FileNotFoundError; the committed table had not been regenerated since the layout move.

_pick_name skipped any GUID-shaped run and kept looking. A BRACE belongs to the same descriptor and must be skipped, but a PLAIN dashed GUID is another descriptor's id, so the name further back is not this type's. Conflating them is how wire 449 stole 'AddActorMessage' from slot 121.
a printable run clipped by the 0x100 window, or split by PRINTABLE_RE's 110-char cap, was accepted as a name. That is where the fragment 'cc8a' came from for slot 0x5d1.

GUID_RE accepted only lowercase, so a type registered with an UPPERCASE dashed GUID was never indexed and its name belonged to nobody; a GUID up to 0xd0 bytes further along then picked it up. That is the root cause behind most of the 39 moved names.
wire-type-names.json.case_and_brace_rule: Case is the discriminator, measured on this image. A lowercase braced GUID IS a registration (<name> NUL <cvar> NUL {695842bb-...} -> slot 5037, PlayerArenaComponentServerFacet_RequestRemoteEnterDungeon). An UPPERCASE braced GUID is AZ's rendering of a GUID inside another descriptor's text (PingMsg NUL {85C7E01E-...} NUL <plain guid>) and must NOT be indexed, or it claims PingMsg and leaves wire 349 unnamed. The all-zero GUID is padding and is always skipped.
wire-type-names.json.removed_fragments_sample: fdbae321d062, cc8a, f5de, pgRA, rqA, e18de33a0e75, erridesDebugTrait, leFromClientFacet, ientRequestUnstuck, tingReady, essages::State, Data, options, BodyComponent.
wire-type-names.json.gained_confirmation: slots 2 and 19 now resolve to RegistrationRequestV2Msg and RegistrationRequestV3Msg, and slot 3 to RegistrationResponseMsg - the registration rungs, previously unnamed
wire-type-names.json.tests: reverse/tools/tests/test_scan_wire_names.py, 20 tests, including 5 new regressions for the four defects; the three committed-artifact guards had been raising FileNotFoundError (ROOT.parents[2] was one level too high) and now actually run

scan-client-facets.py.state: FIXED for 1.460 â€” tables=369 named=369, 368 distinct names identical character-for-character to the 1.400 artifact
scan-client-facets.py.root_cause: Address pinning, not a layout or compiler change. The five-qword descriptor tail [SHARED_A][SHARED_B][FACTORY][SHARED_D][SHARED_E] is unchanged and the factory still has the same CreateByName body, but the four SHARED slots are .text function pointers that move with every build. None of the four 1.400 values occurs anywhere in the 1.460 image (0 raw-qword hits each), so the find() never matched and the tool reported 0 tables on a build that still contains all 368 facets.
scan-client-facets.py.second_bug: resolve_name imported Capstone, which is not installed in .azoth/venv, so even a matching tail would have died with ModuleNotFoundError at the first name. Replaced with a stdlib rip-relative lea/mov reader.
scan-client-facets.py.invariants_kept: EXPECTED_TABLES=369, EXPECTED_DISTINCT=368, all names must be *ClientFacet, all anchor VAs enforced. Nothing was relaxed to make it pass.
scan-client-facets.py.stale_pin_is_dangerous: Old address 0x141698eb0 was a GameRigidBody facet factory in 1.400 and is a live factory in 1.460 for AoiGhostListenTestComponentClientFacet. That is why the scan requires all five words plus the name family and never a partial match.
scan-client-facets.py.still_unknown: The identity and role of the four SHARED slot functions on 1.460 (only observed to be shared .text pointers); 21 further *ClientFacet strings have no table in this family, and the same classes are absent from the 1.400 artifact too, so it is not a 1.460 regression, but their creation path is unknown.

scan-az-types.py (partially).state: FIXED for the field-block form: registry 4781 -> 5109 entries, table-resident 722 -> 939, 328 entries from the 1.460 pointer-field-block form, 0 conflicts, 17 pinned GUIDs reproduce
scan-az-types.py (partially).grammar: In 1.460 a descriptor can be <name>�<pad><k qwords, all in-image .text pointers>�{padded}{GUID}. Measured on GlobalStorageComponentClientFacet_ReceiveStorageSearchItems at 0x8137680: 5 NUL pad, six pointer qwords at 0x81376c0, then {AA0A0B64-...} at 0x81376f0 = typeindex[7048]. k is variable, observed 0..28, capped at 32.
scan-az-types.py (partially).why_a_naive_rule_is_wrong: Accidental adjacency is real: FxScriptsData at 0x85f4250 is followed by 331 qwords and then a GUID the type table does not know. The adopted rule needs all four conditions (maximal in-image-pointer run before an 8-byte-aligned brace, preceded by >=1 NUL, k <= 32, whole NUL-terminated identifier-shaped name on an 8-byte boundary) plus a no-rename guard.
scan-az-types.py (partially).trust_audit: Of the added pairs the independent .rdata route can check, 12 of 13 agree; the pre-existing NUL form scores 58 of 60 under the same test.
scan-az-types.py (partially).still_unrecoverable: 110 of the 4818 1.400 pairs, cause measured per pair: 38 the 1.460 image only has the brace before the first occurrence of that name, 33 another {GUID} sits between name and brace, 26 the interstice is neither NULs nor an all-pointer block, 8 the brace GUID is absent from 1.460, 5 other. At wire level that leaves 37 rows unnamed.

build_delta_1_400_to_1_460.registry_diff: 13 message names present in the 1.460 registry and absent from the committed 1.400 registry, 10 the reverse, 134 in both
build_delta_1_400_to_1_460.caveat: That difference is a difference between two REGISTRY SCANS, not a proven protocol change. client-functions.json records a whole-image scan that found 156 name+GUID pairs, while the registry holds 144 (old) and 147 (new), so the registry is a filtered subset and its coverage may differ between runs.

ReceiveActorMsg.discriminator: The GUIDs are different, and BOTH exist in the 1.460 type table (index 921 holds 764599E8, index 522 holds B232749E). So this is not a shifted index: either the message type identity changed between builds, or the name-to-GUID pairing drifted. Not yet resolved.

build_delta_1_400_to_1_460.needed_to_resolve: Decompile the descriptor getter for ReceiveActorMsg on 1.460 and read which GUID it registers, the same way client-functions.json resolved the movement family. That needs a Ghidra project for this build, which does not exist yet.

capture_purity.statement: pktmon runs with --comp nics, so a session pcap contains every flow on the machine, not only the game's. Measured on live_20261022_r1460_first: after the SNI fix the pcap named api.github.com, code.verboo.ai, telemetry.gentlemanprogramming.com, ecs.office.com, api.steampowered.com and store.steampowered.com, none of which the game contacts.
capture_purity.consequence: Flow attribution must be filtered by the game's PID connections or by the game's own host list before any traffic is treated as protocol evidence. A top-IP table from a raw pcap is not a game-flow table.
capture_purity.corrected_claim: The 22,273-packet TCP flow to 51.222.108.239 was first read as voice/Vivox from its OVH reverse DNS. With SNI extraction fixed it is code.verboo.ai, an agent-tooling host. The reverse-DNS inference was wrong.

live_run_2026_10_25_private_client.why: First attempt to drive the ladder live on the installed 1.460 build. It did not reach WaitingForREPConnection, and the failure is recorded because the diagnostic path is worth keeping.
live_run_2026_10_25_private_client.method: python ef.py dev (caddy + gateway + world) then EF game start; passive Game.log only, no debugger attached to the client by hand

with_launcher_patches.outcome: the private client dies at ~20-25 s, twice measured (alive 6-21 s, then 4-22 s)
with_launcher_patches.reached: Steam auth, world metadata, entitlements, 'Channel Service data provider: init success'
dead_ends_ruled_out: the IapClient failure itself: builds.json already records it as one of five errors present in a CLEAN OFFICIAL session, so it is benign
GPU absence: the log says '- Suitable rendering device: yes' for Intel(R) HD Graphics 630, the same verdict the working official session got, and 2 'Displays connected: yes' lines match
the launcher killing it: Start-NwPrivate.ps1 only Stop-Processes the child on EAC/private-process validation failures or a missing venv, neither of which fired
a missing lab: the same failure happens with caddy+gateway+world confirmed running

without_launcher_patches.outcome: the client SURVIVES past the point where the patched run dies and reaches authentication
auth_trace: [OmniAuthBackend] Omni CreateSession complete with result: 201, id: (EMPTY)
[SteamAuth] Failed to create session for Omni, result code: 201
[AuthStackCredentialsProvider] Failed to get valid gateway AWS credentials
without_launcher_patches.reading: 201 with an empty id is not success. Whatever serves Omni CreateSession answered without an id, the client treated that as failure, and Persona auth never started.

gateway_side.observed: the gateway received only configuration-set GETs (/applications/public..., /applications/publicGameplay..., /motd/worlds_STEAM_APP_ID.json). It logged NO auth POST, so the auth exchange either went to the real Amazon endpoints or was refused before reaching the gateway.
gateway_side.consequence: the next step is not about the game at all: find where the client sends its Omni and Steam auth, confirm whether Caddy routed it to the gateway, and why the Omni mock answers 201 with no id.

live_run_2026_10_25_private_client.hosts_already_configured: C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts already maps 26 Amazon and cloudfront hostnames to 127.0.0.1 for caddy, so no elevation is needed and that was never the blocker.

root_cause_found.finding: deploy/Caddyfile.json dialed 127.0.0.1:8082 for the whole auth/API hostname set. 8082 was the deleted Rust regiond's port; commit f05c3e1 moved that route there and the Rust removal left it pointing at nothing.
root_cause_found.how_it_hid: Caddy answered 502 while `ef.py status` reported 'gateway: running'. A dial failure is invisible in the status, and a timeout reads exactly like a game problem.
root_cause_found.proof: before: GET https://tokenservice.amazongames.com/ -> 502 and POST https://d1w0bfy6smo4d1.cloudfront.net/games/new-world/tokens -> 502. After the one-line fix: 404 on the root and 200 on the tokens POST, and the gateway log shows 'POST /games/new-world/tokens 2B -> omni tokens mock'. Hostnames were never the problem: Caddy declares 34 and /etc/hosts maps all 34 to 127.0.0.1.

remaining_failure.where: between the enum-registration warning and the IapClient line
remaining_failure.symptom: the client writes the EnumStringConversion warning at +0.374 s after 'Channel Service data provider: init success' and then dies writing nothing else
remaining_failure.why_it_is_local: the official working 1.460 session took 14 s to reach the SAME 'Fuel::Iap::IapClient: 14' line and then continued to 'Initializing default materials', the level load and InGame. A local, deterministic exit that fast is not that delay, so IapClient is a coincidence, not the cause.
ruled_out: auth routing: fixed in a44c425, tokens POST returns 200 with a well-formed body
the auth body: _token_set() emits every field the SDK reads, in the field order its docstring requires
GPU absence: 'Suitable rendering device: yes' for Intel HD 630, same as the official session
IapClient itself: builds.json already records it as present in a clean official session
remaining_failure.next_diagnostic: capture the process's last moments instead of its log: run the private exe under 'az.py'/'ef.py' style instrumentation with a WER local dump configured (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\LocalDumps), or check CrashDB for a fresh report. CrashDB/reports was empty for every attempt so far, so the client is exiting through a path that does not raise a crash report.
